internal.title: High Kafka Consumer Lag and Latency in Accounting Service Resolved
internal.body:
At 12:06 UTC, an alert for high Kafka consumer lag was received for the accounting service. Initial diagnosis at 12:26 identified high latency and a backlog in Kafka consumer processing as the primary issues. The consumer lag reached 5200 records, and p95 latency was elevated at 0.12 seconds.

The ops team proposed and executed disabling a specific flag related to Kafka queue problems at 12:26, which was approved by the evaluation on-call engineer. Following this action, latency metrics stabilized, confirming recovery.

No direct evidence of resource exhaustion was found, but it remains a potential contributing factor. The incident was resolved promptly with no further impact observed.

Timeline:
- 12:06 Alert received
- 12:26 Diagnosis and flag disable action
- 12:26 Recovery verified

Next steps include monitoring Kafka consumer lag closely and investigating potential resource constraints further if similar issues recur.

external.title: Intermittent Processing Delays in Accounting Service Resolved
external.body: Between 12:06 and 12:26 UTC, the accounting service experienced intermittent processing delays due to a backlog in message consumption from Kafka. This caused slower response times temporarily. The issue was identified and resolved by adjusting internal processing flags, restoring normal service performance. We continue to monitor the system to prevent recurrence.
